name: IBM 5151 monochrome display, P39 green phosphor (MDA raster)

timing.ref: IBM BIOS 6845 parameters for the MDA (R0 61h, R4 19h, R5 06h, R9 0Dh) and the 16.257 MHz dot clock; 5151: 50 Hz, 18.432 kHz, 350 lines (Wikipedia, IBM 5151)

drive.mapping: level = floor(3 (1 - luma) + 0.5) / 3: dark art drives the beam
drive.ref: MDA video pin = 2/3, intensity pin = 1/3 of the luminance (Wikipedia, IBM Monochrome Display Adapter). Content is free, so the TTL signal may switch anywhere along a line.

layers.name: green
layers.display_note: outside sRGB: shown on the display's green primary at its true luminance

facts: P39 (Zn2SiO4:Mn,As), 525 nm, x 0.205 y 0.715 (Philips). Outside sRGB: shown on the display's green primary
builds up for 12 ms, 10% after 106 ms, 1% after 372 ms; JEDEC class long (100 ms-1 s)
Mn2+ decay from P1 (20 ms to 10%) fed by bimolecular trap release (IBM, 1985), its time solved from P39's measured 30 Hz flicker ratio (US 4,315,190)
refs: Philips T16 1987 survey of screen phosphors (GR = P39: x 0.205, y 0.715; long = 100 ms-1 s)
Juestel, CRT Phosphors (P39 Zn2SiO4:Mn,As, 525 nm, long)
Jankowiak, CRT phosphors of interest to the experimenter (P1: 20 ms to 10 %, exponential)
Robbins, Caswell, Avouris, Giess, Chang, Dove, J. Electrochem. Soc. 1985 (bimolecular trap recombination in Zn2SiO4:Mn,As)
US 4,315,190 table 1 (commercial P39 ripple ratio 0.370 at 30 Hz)

colour.note: P39 lies outside sRGB (red and blue would be negative). Shown on the sRGB green primary at the correct luminance; above the display's maximum green it clips, keeping the hue: a P39 screen never looks white.

spot.ref: Philips M31-336/338/350: about 1300 lines over 201 mm (shrinking raster, 68.5 cd/m2); flat-field pitch = 2 sigma

raster.note: raster assumed to fill the useful height of a Philips 31 cm 90 degree monitor tube; the 5151's own picture size is not published

faceplate.ref: Philips T16 1987: light transmission about 50 % (normal tint), etched anti-glare option

contrast.note: video gain (IBM: 'increases the brightness of the data')

brightness.note: uniform beam on every line (IBM: 'increases the brightness of the entire screen'); fraction of full drive
